overall: The AG found the Lenox Select Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the March 29 minutes were accurate and sufficient, and the public-comment claim was declined because it would not be a violation even if true.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 29 minutes omitted how to request reasonable accommodations, who the ADA officer is, and the time-sensitivity before Town Meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the minutes relative to the subject raised by Ms. Bykofsky were accurate and sufficiently detailed, and satisfied the Board's obligations under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not allow public comment following a Planning Board presentation at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the allegation that the Board did not allow public comment following the Planning Board's presentation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law in any event, we decline to review this allegation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
